content: CLI commands are one-file-per-command under src/cli/commands/<name>.ts. Each exports run(ctx: CliContext) => Promise<number> and parses its own argv with a command-local ArgSpec via parseArgs(). The router (src/cli/router.ts) is a flat dispatch table that owns global --help/--version and converts thrown errors into stderr + exit code 1 (PLOT_DEBUG=1 surfaces stack traces). The shared runtime (src/cli/runtime.ts) provides parseArgs, CliIO/CliEnv interfaces, resolveActor (PLOT_ACTOR env wins, falls back to user:<git user.email handle>), resolveStoreEnv (PLOT_DIR or .plot), and withStore() which builds a PlotStore+SQLitePlotIndex and closes the index in finally. Tests drive the router with captured IO and a fake CliEnv against a temp PLOT_DIR — no process globals, no real git config dependency.

name: agent-cli-plot-id-resolution
description: Agent-facing CLI commands (plot get / plot append) resolve the target Plot ID from three sources in priority order: positional arg, --plot flag, then PLOT_ID env var. Implemented as resolvePlotId() in src/cli/runtime.ts and shared by both commands so the agent CLI surface stays uniform. Throws with a 'no Plot ID — pass <id>, --plot <id>, or set PLOT_ID' message that command handlers convert into an exit-2 usage error.

content: plot append rejects events that have dedicated subcommands (intent_edited, status_changed, attachment_added/removed, question_answered, plot_created) with a CLI-level redirect to the correct subcommand. For agent actors, the ACL check fires first and surfaces the SPEC §6 'use question_posed instead' hint per acl.ts REDIRECT_HINT — so the order in src/cli/commands/append.ts matters: ACL check first, dedicated-command redirect second.

name: doctor-replay-validation
description: plot doctor validates each Plot by replaying the event log (status_changed, intent_edited, attachment_added/removed) and comparing the reconstructed state to the on-disk JSON. Divergence becomes an error finding (status_drift, attachments_drift) or warning (intent_drift). Also surfaces malformed JSON, malformed JSONL, unknown event types, invalid actors/timestamps, and orphan events.jsonl files lacking a sibling pl-xxxx.json. Exit code 1 on any error, 0 on warnings only. --json emits a structured DoctorReport for tooling.

name: acceptance-driven-integration-tests
description: Integration tests live in src/integration.test.ts and exercise the SPEC §3 acceptance criteria of a plan end-to-end: drive runCli with captured IO and an in-memory env against a mkdtemp PLOT_DIR. Per-command behavior stays in cli/router.test.ts; the integration suite walks complete scenarios across module boundaries (human authoring, agent ACL redirect, rebuild-index round-trip, migrate-on-read, implementer view shape) so the surface stays coherent.

content: Release prep workflow: bump via "bun run scripts/version-bump.ts <major|minor|patch>" (updates package.json + src/version.ts atomically), then move CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entries under a dated [version] heading, then verify with "bun test && bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun publish --dry-run" before committing as "chore: release v<version>". Do not push or tag from the release commit itself.

name: l5-ratchet-script-porting
description: Ported L5 file-size + debt-marker ratchets from templates/l5-toolkit verbatim. Budgets are baselined per the porting playbook: file-size threshold stays at the ecosystem-standard 500 with files over it grandfathered at their current line count (src/cli/router.test.ts:834, src/store.test.ts:598) rather than raising the global cap. Debt-marker trackerPatterns are plot-specific (pl-XXXX/mx-XXXX, #NNN, URL) — distinct from seeds IDs which are plot-XXXX. Ported scripts trip biome's noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity; resolve by adding the script paths to biome.json's existing complexity override (canopy precedent) rather than refactoring upstream toolkit code.
